speaker: Avery Santana
cascadeSummary: Oakland's hearing agenda puts delivery and proof side by side: West Oakland charter renewal, the Fruitvale alternative-response briefing, Temescal audits, apprenticeship corrections, recorded Grand Lake and tenant-defense decisions, and verified Laurel legislation. I am holding Baylight and Fruitvale Transit Hub milestones to evidence, withdrawing the unverified INIT-014 filing claim, and committing to a ten-complaint, seven-response crosswalk because the packet supplies no docket or Clerk references. Glenview and Piedmont Avenue get bounded service follow-up, Ivy Hill and San Antonio get attention without a manufactured crisis, and Oakland's block parties remain part of the city's life.

statements.topic: Petition ledger crosswalk and INIT-014 filing correction
statements.decision: On Planning Director Mara Vance's Cycle 116 directive (P-d94459ae1189b667; P-b87ef751a66c370d) and Decision 9, withdraw the unverified C115 INIT-014 filing claim and hold filed-legislation review until the Clerk supplies a reference. Publish a ten-complaint, seven-response crosswalk with each response docket, covered complaint IDs, responsible office, proposed remedy and next date, plus the status of every uncovered complaint. The packet lacks the ledger and all references, so no docket or Clerk number is asserted in this agenda statement.
statements.quote: I will not turn seven responses into ten resolved complaints, or call INIT-014 filed, without docket and Clerk evidence.
statements.fullStatement: Oaklanders deserve a record that reconciles, not seven response claims floating beside ten complaints. Planning Director Mara Vance is right to demand the crosswalk. My packet does not include the complaint ledger, the seven docket references, or a Clerk reference for INIT-014, so I will not invent them. I will publish a crosswalk with Planning and the Clerk identifying each complaint covered by each response, every responsible office, proposed remedy and next date, and the status of every complaint left uncovered. I am also withdrawing my C115 filing statement: INIT-014's filing is not verified. The live tracker still lists it announced, with filing past due from C114. Until the Clerk supplies a reference, Council review of filed legislation is not accurate. Ivy Hill's low crime, slow trade and soured mood remain the proposal's premise, not a manufactured emergency.

statements.topic: West Oakland Stabilization Fund charter renewal
statements.decision: On Cycle 116 Pending Decisions Packet, Decision 1, place the $28 million fund's charter renewal on this cycle's council agenda. Support renewal only with its West Oakland business-and-resident scope and 23-day processing standard intact, and require the ordered C114 closeout publication in the hearing record before a final renewal decision.
statements.quote: Renewal means West Oakland businesses and residents, a 23-day standard, and a public closeout record before Council makes its decision.
statements.fullStatement: West Oakland built this fund's case, and West Oakland remains its purpose. I am putting the $28 million charter renewal on this cycle's council agenda with the business-and-resident scope intact and the 23-day processing standard preserved. Downtown is outside this fund; INIT-008 remains proposed, not voted. Before Council makes a final renewal decision, the ordered closeout publication must be in the hearing record so members can judge results rather than my assurances. I hear the demand for accountability, and I welcome it: renewal should protect what works, identify what needs correction, and leave a public record of both. Transmittal is not passage, and I will not describe it that way.

statements.topic: Fruitvale alternative-response briefing and expansion hold
statements.decision: On Cycle 116 Pending Decisions Packet, Decision 2, hold expansion and calendar completion of the D3 Fruitvale briefing this cycle, including district-level and Fruitvale data, documented community participation, and publication of the briefing record. Require responsible next dates for the still-incomplete D5 audit and Baylight feasibility review.
statements.quote: Fruitvale gets data, a real briefing, and a published record before Oakland considers expanding alternative response.
statements.fullStatement: Oakland's alternative-response work should expand only when the evidence and the neighborhood briefing support it. I am holding expansion and putting the D3 Fruitvale briefing on this cycle's action calendar: conduct it, document who participated and what was asked, and publish district-level and Fruitvale data. The D5 audit and Baylight feasibility review also remain incomplete, so the record must give their responsible next dates rather than imply they are finished. This is a $12.5 million initiative, and trust is part of the delivery. Fruitvale gets the briefing before any expansion decision, not a presentation after the decision has already been made.

statements.initiative: Fruitvale Transit Hub Phase II — Visioning
statements.decision: On Cycle 116 Pending Decisions Packet, Decision 3, let the engine flag pass without new phase or funding action because C115 is closed and the flag identifies low-severity improvement. Preserve the C86 authorization history, but gate any future design advancement on delivered preliminary schematics and a documented Fruitvale public comment-and-response record.
statements.quote: A transit hub earns its next design step through delivered schematics and answers to Fruitvale, not through a calendar reminder.
statements.fullStatement: Fruitvale's $230 million transit-hub authorization is part of this city's commitment to connect neighborhoods to opportunity, but a low-severity improvement flag is not a design milestone. I am taking no new phase or funding action on this item this cycle. Before any further design advancement, the record must contain the preliminary schematics and a documented Fruitvale community review, including public comments and responses. The C86 council authorization belongs in the history accurately, and so does the C115 closure; neither lets me skip the public record. When those materials are ready, residents should be able to see what changed because they spoke.

statements.decision: On Cycle 116 Pending Decisions Packet, Decision 4, keep the open center on its standing oversight schedule by calendaring the Q3 intake-audit filing to HCAI and the Council Clerk and the recurring Telegraph and 47th merchant-clinic verification walkthrough this cycle. Publish completion and findings afterward; claim neither as complete now.
statements.quote: Temescal's health center stays accountable through quarterly audits and verification walks, not through memories of an opening ceremony.
statements.fullStatement: Oakland's Temescal Community Health Center is open, and the job now is to prove every quarter that it serves people well. I am keeping the Q3 intake audit and the Telegraph and 47th merchant-clinic verification walkthrough on this cycle's calendar. The audit is due to HCAI and the Council Clerk under the standing schedule, and the walkthrough should produce a public completion record and any corrective findings. The center opened ahead of schedule and $1.2 million under budget; that is a strong start, not a reason to relax oversight. Councilmember Ashford's audit concerns deserve a standing answer through routine verification, not a one-time defense.

statements.topic: Baylight evidence-file review and construction oversight
statements.decision: On Cycle 116 Pending Decisions Packet, Decision 5, let the low-severity Jack London and Downtown improvement flags pass without declaring a construction milestone passed or claiming a final vote. Continue remediation, independent oversight, the 48-hour hotline, dust control and workforce oversight, and require a public evidence-file determination before any future milestone decision.
statements.quote: At Baylight, oversight documents must carry the weight of the next milestone; upbeat street conditions cannot do that work for them.
statements.fullStatement: Baylight is a $2.1 billion commitment, and Oakland will not confuse busy Downtown streets with a passed construction milestone. I am making no milestone-pass or final-vote claim this cycle. Independent remediation verification, the 48-hour hotline record, dust control on haul routes, and Jack London workforce results belong in one public evidence file, with a clear determination of what has and has not been met. Remediation and independent oversight continue while that record is tested. The low-severity improvement flags in Jack London and Downtown are welcome, but they are not engineering evidence. Baylight moves on verified work, and the public gets the evidence before the celebration.

statements.topic: Youth apprenticeship placement gaps and required disposition
statements.decision: On Cycle 116 Pending Decisions Packet, Decision 6, require publication this cycle of the placement-gap analysis and adjustment plan, including explicit West Oakland and Fruitvale reviews, who placements reach, specific corrections, responsible owners and next reporting dates. Put a binary disposition on the hearing agenda after publication: evidence-supported advancement or a recorded fail if the required materials remain undelivered, with no automatic hold.
statements.quote: This apprenticeship hearing ends in evidence and a disposition: published gaps, specific corrections, then advancement on results or failure on the record.
statements.fullStatement: Oakland's young people need placements they can reach, not another cycle of implementation language. I am putting the $12.5 million apprenticeship pipeline's gap analysis and adjustment plan on the floor for publication this cycle, with explicit reviews of West Oakland and Fruitvale, who is actually receiving placements, and what will change. Every adjustment needs a responsible owner and a next reporting date. After four cycles in the same stage, I will not accept an automatic hold: if the required analysis and plan are not delivered, the hearing should record failure; if they are, any advancement must still rest on the evidence.

statements.decision: On Cycle 116 Pending Decisions Packet, Decision 7, keep the scheduled recorded full-council vote on this cycle's agenda and back YES on the $2.5 million proposal. Require every Chen-Vega milestone and audit condition to remain attached and ask the Clerk to certify the roll call, without forecasting the outcome.
statements.quote: The Grand Lake decision will live in the Clerk's roll call, with milestones and audits written into the result rather than appended later.
statements.fullStatement: Grand Lake's busy street trade is an opportunity to act carefully, not an excuse to blur the legislative record. I am keeping the $2.5 million Commercial Stabilization proposal's scheduled full-council decision on this cycle's agenda, and my position is yes. Every Chen-Vega milestone and audit condition stays attached; those safeguards are part of the proposal, not decorations to be removed after the vote. I ask the Clerk to certify the roll call so residents can see exactly where each member stood. I respect colleagues who want proof before celebration. If it passes, those conditions govern implementation; if it fails, the public will still have an honest decision and a clear basis for the next step.

statements.topic: West Oakland tenant-defense analysis before committee decision
statements.decision: On Cycle 116 Pending Decisions Packet, Decision 8, keep the scheduled committee decision on the agenda but sequence it behind publication of the legal-support analysis. No vote should occur before that analysis is public; afterward, the Housing and Community Development Committee should record its decision on the $4.2 million proposal without any outcome presumed.
statements.quote: The sequence matters: West Oakland gets the legal analysis first and a recorded committee judgment second, with no outcome scripted in between.
statements.fullStatement: West Oakland residents are entitled to see the legal analysis before anyone asks a committee to decide. I am sequencing this cycle's Housing and Community Development Committee agenda accordingly: publish the legal-support analysis first, allow members and the public to examine it, then record the committee's decision on the $4.2 million tenant-defense proposal. I am not announcing approval, rejection, or a vote count today. The analysis should explain the proposed legal support, delivery responsibilities, and accountability measures so the decision rests on evidence. Denise Carter has consistently pressed me to value residents' voices; this process should reflect that by making the basis for the vote public before the gavel falls.

statements.topic: Laurel cleanup legislation and verified filing
statements.decision: On Cycle 116 Pending Decisions Packet, Decision 10, keep INIT-015 accurately described as announced and place completed drafting and Clerk-verified filing on this cycle's required agenda. The $6 million legislation must define cleanup scope, direct neighborhood outreach, visible follow-through and maintenance responsibilities; if verification is not obtained, record the filing deadline as missed rather than claiming success.
statements.quote: A Laurel cleanup becomes real through a defined scope, resident outreach, and a Clerk entry neighbors can verify for themselves.
statements.fullStatement: Laurel needs a cleanup plan that residents can recognize on their own blocks. I am putting the $6 million proposal's drafting and Clerk-verified filing on this cycle's calendar, with a defined cleanup scope, direct neighborhood outreach, visible follow-through, and clear maintenance responsibilities. My office's words will not substitute for the Clerk's record. If the legislation is not actually filed and verified, I will say the deadline was missed rather than relabel an announcement as progress. Laurel's mildly positive mood and slow trade call for practical follow-through, not an inflated emergency. The next public update should show the scope, what residents asked for, and the verified filing status.

statements.topic: Neighborhood conditions, service follow-up and civic life
statements.decision: On Cycle 116 Pending Decisions Packet, Decision 11 and the City This Cycle incident record, request public status reports from the responsible departments on Glenview's medium-severity public-works spike and Piedmont Avenue's medium-severity health spike, identifying what happened, what has been resolved and the next update date. Pair direct listening in Ivy Hill with attention to San Antonio's struggling trade, without authorizing new spending or declaring a broader emergency.
statements.quote: Public-works answers in Glenview, health answers on Piedmont Avenue, and room for three block parties: that is responsive city government.
statements.fullStatement: Oakland can respond to problems without turning the whole city into a crisis. I am asking the responsible departments for public status reports on Glenview's medium-severity public-works spike and Piedmont Avenue's medium-severity health spike: what happened, what has been resolved, and when neighbors get the next update. I also want direct listening in Ivy Hill, where the mood has soured and trade is slow, and attention to San Antonio's struggling street trade. Those are different conditions requiring different responses. Meanwhile, West Oakland, Fruitvale and other neighborhoods are upbeat, crime is low across the listed neighborhoods, and the Kelley, Horn and Keane family block parties matter. Civic joy is not a distraction from delivery; it is part of the city we are delivering for.
